approach: The `athena` binary doubles as a `cargo` shim, as it already does for `pre-commit` and `commit-msg` (main.rs:551). In `producer_loop`, right after the existing `self.agent_spec(..)` call for `Role::Producer` (producer.rs:192-207), the loop builds a `CargoShim` and calls `install` then `apply` on `spec.env`. So reading.rs, which builds every role's spec, is left alone (finding 1). `install` makes `<job_dir>/shim/cargo`, a symlink to `self.athena_bin`. `apply` puts that directory first on the producer's PATH and sets the slot variables. The slot variables carry the slots dir, slot count, promote seconds, the wait limit and the wait-note path. `env::build` and `EnvSpec` are untouched, so the verifier and checks keep their environments. The wrapper's wait is capped below the Bash timeout (finding 2): `shim_wait_s = min(build_wait_s, max(1, bash_default_timeout_ms / 2000))`. With the shipped athena.toml (600000 ms) that is min(1800, 300) = 300 s, so the wrapper gives up with its message and note while the agent's Bash call is still alive, and the build keeps half of the Bash budget. When `main` sees argv[0] == `cargo` it calls `slot_exec::run`. That finds the subcommand with `policy::cargo_subcommand`, which shares one helper with `check_cargo` (finding 4). For build, test, clippy and check it takes a `Class::Producer` slot from a `SlotQueue` over the shared slots dir. It then runs the real cargo (PATH minus the shim dir) and frees the slot when cargo exits. On `SlotWait` it prints `no build slot free for <limit> s; try again`, writes a wait note under the job dir and exits 75 without starting cargo. After a successful producer invocation, `producer_loop` finds the note and returns the `SlotWait` as an error. `produce_and_verify` turns that into `hold_for_slot_wait`, so the job is held as `environment: build slot wait` with no outcome and no attempt used. The retry fixes stay: `athena-cli --test slot_exec` is registered in xtask/shard-timings.txt, a fmt/metadata no-slot test is kept, and the criteria cite runnable commands.

decisions.choice: One binary dispatched on argv[0] == `cargo`, reached through a `<job_dir>/shim/cargo` symlink, not a `build-slot -- <cmd>` subcommand. The design doc says so.
decisions.reason: The producer types plain `cargo ...` and the policy checks it by name (policy.rs refuses a path-qualified program). A PATH shim leaves the agent's commands and the policy as they are. main.rs:551 already dispatches on argv[0]. This is the candidate design of the earlier job, accepted in the reading.

rejected.option: A `build-slot -- <cmd>` subcommand as in design doc section 6 step 4
rejected.why: The agent would have to type it, the policy would have to allow it and parse the inner command, which makes a second parser for cargo commands.
A second file format outside the SlotQueue, so no class order, ageing or SlotWait; all code is Rust.

decisions.choice: Apply the shim in `producer_loop` on `spec.env` after `agent_spec`, not inside `agent_spec` (answers finding 1).
decisions.reason: producer.rs is a listed deliverable and already mutates the producer's spec there (`spec.effort`, producer.rs:209-211). It is the only place that builds a producer spec (producer.rs:192), so the shim reaches the producer only, and reading.rs (not a deliverable) stays unchanged. `agent_spec`'s other callers (planning.rs, verification.rs, auditor.rs, pin.rs, steward.rs, hestia.rs, audience.rs, reading.rs) never see it.

rejected.option: Add the shim inside `agent_spec` guarded by `role == Role::Producer`
rejected.why: Edits reading.rs, which is outside the listed deliverables, and puts producer-only code in the code every role shares.

decisions.choice: The wrapper's wait is `min(build_wait_s, max(1, bash_default_timeout_ms / 2000))`, computed once by `CargoShim::new` in env.rs and passed to the wrapper in an env var. The design doc records the choice and its reason, and says section 4's 1800 s still governs the checks' wait.
decisions.reason: athena.toml:64-65 sets the Bash default timeout to 600000 ms and the maximum to 1200000 ms, and config.rs:166 defaults build_wait_s to 1800. A wrapper waiting 1800 s would be killed by Bash at 600 s, so no message, note or hold would ever occur, and the wait would eat the build's own time. Half of the Bash default (300 s for the shipped config) is long enough to queue and leaves the rest for the build. Needs no athena.toml edit (governance). A unit test reads the shipped athena.toml and asserts the shim's wait is below the Bash default timeout.

rejected.option: Keep build_wait_s (1800 s) in the wrapper
rejected.why: The Bash call is killed first, so criterion 3's behavior cannot happen in production.

rejected.option: Edit athena.toml's Bash timeouts or build_wait_s
rejected.why: A governance file, not a deliverable.

rejected.option: Pass both values and let the wrapper take the minimum
rejected.why: The wrapper would need the config rules; computing it once in env.rs keeps one definition, tested against the shipped file.

decisions.choice: One shared helper in policy.rs finds the subcommand; both `check_cargo` and `cargo_subcommand` call it (answers finding 4). `CARGO_GLOBAL_FLAGS` becomes `pub`. The helper takes the words as an iterator of `&str` and returns an enum: `Sub { index, word }`, `UnknownFlag(flag)` or `NoSub`. It skips leading dash words that are in the list. `check_cargo` maps `UnknownFlag` and `NoSub` to its current error strings, byte for byte, and uses `index` for `args[i + 1..]`. `pub fn cargo_subcommand(args: &[&str]) -> Option<&str>` returns the word for `Sub` and None otherwise.
decisions.reason: One list and one walk, so the wrapper and the policy cannot drift (criterion 7). The error text stays exact, so the existing check_cargo tests still guard it.

decisions.choice: The host reads the wrapper's wait through a note file `<job_dir>/slot-wait.json` holding the `SlotWait` JSON (SlotWait is Serialize and Deserialize, Copy, disk.rs:275). Helpers go in slots.rs: `wait_note_path`, `write_wait_note`, `read_wait_note`, `clear_wait_note`. `producer_loop` clears the note before each producer invocation. After the Success branch (producer.rs:240-247) it reads the note and returns `Err(wait.into())`. `produce_and_verify` (mod.rs:1492) matches the result and, for a SlotWait error, returns `Err(self.hold_for_slot_wait(ctx, closing, wait))`. The wrapper clears the note whenever it later gets a slot.
decisions.reason: The wrapper is a separate process inside the agent, so a file under the job's own directory is the only channel. The hold path is the one the disk gate already uses before the producer (mod.rs:1476-1477) and the checks use (mod.rs:1669), with no new Flow variant. A producer that retries and gets a slot is not held, because the note is cleared.

rejected.option: Exit 75 only and leave the job to the verifier
rejected.why: The verifier would judge unbuilt work and the job would fail; criterion 3 needs a hold.
Every match on Flow in mod.rs would change.

rejected.option: Check the note after TimedOut or a failed invocation too
rejected.why: Those paths close with kept work or a failure reason and stay as they are.

decisions.choice: The wrapper runs the real cargo as a child with the shim dir stripped from PATH and inherited stdio, holds the slot until the child exits, and returns the child's code (128+signal for a signal). It does not exec.
decisions.reason: A nested cargo started by the real cargo would otherwise re-enter the shim and wait for the slot its parent holds, a deadlock with one slot. The workspace sets `unsafe_code = deny`, so the lock fd cannot be passed to an exec'd cargo.

rejected.option: exec the real cargo, keeping the lock fd
rejected.why: Needs fcntl, so unsafe or a new dependency.

rejected.option: Leave the shim on PATH for the child

risks.risk: A wrapper killed with SIGKILL could leave its child cargo running after the slot lock is freed, so more builds than slots run for a while. The workspace denies `unsafe`, so the lock fd cannot be passed to the child.
risks.mitigation: The Bash timeout and the kill switch end the agent's process group, which includes the child. The window is small. Not fixed here; named in the design doc.

risks.risk: The Bash call could still be killed before the wrapper's wait ends if the agent passes a short explicit timeout, or if the build itself needs more than the remaining half of the default timeout.
risks.mitigation: The cap leaves half of the default (300 s) for the build; the agent may raise its timeout up to the 1200 s maximum for long builds. The design doc names the limit. athena.toml is not edited.

risks.risk: A producer that gives up after a wait loses its run: the job is held and a later drain retries from the base, spending the producer's money again.
risks.mitigation: The hold is applied only when the note is still present after the final command, so a producer that retries and gets a slot is not held. The wait is 300 s in the shipped config before the producer is told to try again.

risks.risk: A stale note from an earlier invocation could hold a job wrongly.
risks.mitigation: `producer_loop` clears the note before every producer invocation and the wrapper clears it on any later slot. The core test covers the cleared-note case.

risks.risk: The shim symlink could fail to be created, which would let the producer build with no slot.
risks.mitigation: `install` errors propagate from producer_loop with `?`, so the producer does not start. The error is not ignored.

risks.risk: The fake driver tests use `athena_bin = /bin/false`; the shim then points to it.
risks.mitigation: `install` only creates a symlink and does not require the target to run; the fake driver never executes it. The wrapper tests use the real `CARGO_BIN_EXE_athena`.

risks.risk: Timing-dependent tests could be flaky on a loaded CI machine.
risks.mitigation: Tests use file markers (`started-*`, `release-*`) and `queue.waiting()` polls with a 10 s bound, not fixed sleeps, as slots.rs tests do. The wait-limit tests use a 1 s wait. The shard time is a registered estimate of 8 s, not a measurement.

risks.risk: `cargo run` and `cargo doc` stay outside the slot list although the policy allows them.
risks.mitigation: Matches the brief; the list is one constant and can be extended later.

risks.risk: Refactoring check_cargo to call the shared helper could change an error message or an index.
risks.mitigation: The existing check_cargo tests guard the text; the helper is the same rule moved, and `args[i + 1..]` uses the helper's index.

demonstrations.method: Integration test with the real `athena` binary run as `cargo` through a symlink in a temp shim dir (target `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_athena")`). A fake `cargo` shell script sits after the shim dir on PATH: it writes `started-<tag>`, waits for `release-<tag>`, then exits 0. One slot, a 30 s wait, and the slots dir of a real `SlotQueue` in a tempdir. Start producer process A (`cargo build`) and wait for `started-A`. Start B and poll until `queue.waiting() == 1`, bounded at 10 s. Assert B has no `started-B` and `try_acquire()` is None. Release A, wait for `started-B`, release B. After both exit assert `try_acquire()` is Some.
demonstrations.observes: While A holds the only slot B is queued and has not run; after A's release B runs; both exit 0 and the slot is free again.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the wrapper took no slot, B would write `started-B` while A held and `waiting() == 1` would never be reached. If the slot were not freed at exit, the final `try_acquire` would be None.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point: `slot_exec::run` through the `athena` binary as `cargo` (argv[0] dispatch added by step 5). Fixtures: a real `SlotQueue` over a tempdir (test-created, read with `SlotQueue::try_acquire`, which exists, slots.rs:168) and a fake cargo script that only records and waits. They are injected by building the child's env with the production `CargoShim::apply` (step 3). The fake holds none of the slot logic. The seam is added by steps 3-5 and 9.

demonstrations.method: Same fixtures, one slot. Run `cargo -q build`, then `cargo --locked test`, through the shim. The fake records its argv, writes `started`, waits for `release`. At each `started` assert `try_acquire()` is None. After exit assert `try_acquire()` is Some and the fake received exactly the original argv. The policy unit tests assert `cargo_subcommand(&["-q","build"]) == Some("build")`, `["--locked","test"] == Some("test")`, `["-vv","check"] == Some("check")`, and None for `["--config","x"]` and `[]`. Existing check_cargo tests run in the same module.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test slot_exec global_flags_before_the_subcommand_still_hold_a_slot && cargo test --locked -p athena-agent policy
demonstrations.observes: Both commands hold the slot while the fake runs and free it after; the real cargo gets the arguments unchanged.
demonstrations.fails_without: A lookup of only args[0] sees `-q` or `--locked`, takes no slot, and `try_acquire` returns Some while the fake runs, failing the assert.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points: `slot_exec::run` via the binary as `cargo`, and `athena_agent::policy::cargo_subcommand` (added by step 2). Fixtures as in criterion 1. The seam is added by steps 2-5 and 9.

demonstrations.method: (a) CLI test: settings are one slot and a 1 s wait; the test holds the slot with `try_acquire()` and runs `cargo build` through the shim. Assert exit code 75, stderr exactly `no build slot free for 1 s; try again`, no `started` file from the fake, and `slots::read_wait_note` at the note path returns a SlotWait with `limit_s == 1`. (b) Core test: `athena_with` plus `counting(..)` drive a fake producer whose script, when role is Producer, writes the note with the production helper `slots::write_wait_note` at the path in `spec.env`, as the wrapper would. Call `athena.go(..)`. Assert the error downcasts to SlotWait, the `held       environment: build slot wait` line was printed, the records show no outcome and no score, `read_slot_hold` equals the wait, the verifier ran 0 times, and a retry after the note is gone runs the producer again and lands. A second case: a producer that wrote the note, then a later cargo got a slot and cleared it, is not held. (c) Env unit test: parse the shipped athena.toml (`include_str!("../../../athena.toml")`, `Config::parse`, config.rs:616) and assert `CargoShim::new(..).wait_s` is below `bash_default_timeout_ms / 1000` and equals 300; a small build_wait_s (such as 1) is kept as is.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test slot_exec a_wait_past_the_limit_exits_75_and_never_starts_cargo && cargo test --locked -p athena-core a_producer_whose_last_cargo_waited_out_the_slot_holds_the_job && cargo test --locked -p athena-agent the_shims_wait_is_below_the_bash_timeout_of_the_shipped_config
demonstrations.observes: The wrapper gives the documented message and a non-failure exit, writes a note, and never starts cargo. A job whose producer ended on that note is held as `environment: build slot wait`, not failed, and resumes. In production the wrapper's limit is under the Bash timeout, so this path is reachable before Bash kills the command.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the wrapper's note, the CLI test finds no note. Without the `producer_loop` check, `go` runs the checks and verifier on unbuilt work and the core test sees a verifier run and a closed outcome. Without the cap, the env test fails (1800 is not below 600).
demonstrations.seam: Entry points: `slot_exec::run` through the binary (CLI); `Athena::go` with `producer_loop` and `produce_and_verify` (core, signatures unchanged); `CargoShim::new` (env). Doubles: a real SlotQueue plus a fake cargo script (CLI); the existing `FakeAgentDriver` script via `athena_with`/`counting` (tests.rs:187 and :2152), which writes the note through the production helper so the hold logic is not in the double (core). The shipped config file is the fixture for (c). Steps 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 add the seam; `athena_with`, `counting` and `slot_queue` exist.

demonstrations.method: One slot, a 1 s wait. The test holds the slot with `try_acquire()` and runs `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo metadata --no-deps` through the shim. The fake cargo writes its argv and exits 0. Assert both exit 0, the fake ran with the right argv, no wait note exists, and the slot is still held by the test at the end.
demonstrations.observes: Both commands run to completion with every slot held and take no slot.
demonstrations.fails_without: If every subcommand took a slot, both would wait 1 s, exit 75, never reach the fake and write a note, failing the asserts.
demonstrations.seam: Same as criterion 1: `slot_exec::run` through the binary as `cargo`, a real SlotQueue held by the test, a fake cargo script, env from `CargoShim::apply`. Added by steps 3-5 and 9.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff: `CARGO_GLOBAL_FLAGS` is `pub`, one new helper holds the leading-flag walk, `check_cargo` and `cargo_subcommand` both call it, and `check_cargo`'s error strings are unchanged. Use the Grep tool on crates/athena-cli/src/slot_exec.rs: it calls `cargo_subcommand` and has no flag literal list (`"--locked"` and `"--offline"` are absent). Run the policy tests: the existing check_cargo cases (`listed_git_and_cargo_commands_are_allowed`, the `--target-dir` and `--manifest-path` denials, an unknown global flag error text, `cargo` without a subcommand) plus the new `cargo_subcommand` tests.
demonstrations.command: git diff -- crates/athena-agent/src/policy.rs && cargo test --locked -p athena-agent policy
demonstrations.observes: One list and one walk; check_cargo behavior and its tests are unchanged and pass.
demonstrations.fails_without: A second list in slot_exec.rs would appear in the diff or the Grep. A changed error string or walk in check_cargo breaks its existing tests.

demonstrations.method: The diff shows `build` and `EnvSpec` unchanged, with only `CargoShim` and its helpers added. The core test (narrowed to producer versus verifier, finding 3) uses the existing fake agent Script, which receives an `AgentInvocation`: for the Producer role it records `spec.env`, and for the Verifier role it does too. After `go` it asserts the producer's PATH starts with `<job_dir>/shim` and has the slot variables, and the verifier's env has none of those variables and a PATH equal to the parent's. Checks are not run through the agent driver (checks.rs:556, :826 call `env::build` and run through SnapExec), so for them an env unit test asserts `env::build(..)` output has no `ATHENA_CARGO_SHIM_DIR` or slot variable and PATH is the parent's. The diff shows no change to checks.rs.
demonstrations.command: git diff -- crates/athena-agent/src/env.rs && cargo test --locked -p athena-core only_the_producer_gets_the_cargo_shim_first_on_path && cargo test --locked -p athena-agent build_adds_no_shim_variables
demonstrations.observes: Only the producer's PATH changes; verifier and check environments are as before.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the shim went on every role's PATH, or into `env::build`, the verifier and `build` assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points: `Athena::go`, then `producer_loop` (where the shim is applied) and `verification.rs`'s `agent_spec` call for the verifier; and `env::build`. Double: the existing `FakeAgentDriver` Script capturing `spec.env` (exists); the capture is added by step 8.
